items.title: UK's Cooper demands toll-free Strait of Hormuz passage

featured_image.name: Britain to call for toll-free Strait of Hormuz amid US-Iran ceasefire

items.description:
British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper is set to declare on Thursday that shipping through the Strait of Hormuz must remain free of tolls, directly challenging both Iran's efforts to control the waterway and a suggestion from President Donald Trump to establish a joint toll system for the critical passage.[1][2]

In her annual foreign policy address at Mansion House in London, Cooper will argue that international maritime law forbids levying charges on vessels transiting the strait, which carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas.[3][4]

"The fundamental freedoms of the seas must not be unilaterally withdrawn or sold off to individual bidders. Nor can there be any place for tolls on an international waterway. Freedom of navigation means navigation must be free," Cooper will say, according to advance excerpts of the speech.[4][2]

items.title: Chevron projects up to $2.2B Q1 earnings boost from higher oil prices

featured_image.name: Chevron CEO says Iran war impact isn't fully priced into oil market

items.description:
Chevron said on Thursday that higher commodity prices driven by the war in Iran are expected to lift its first-quarter upstream earnings by $1.6 billion to $2.2 billion compared with the fourth quarter of 2025, even as the conflict cut into the company's global production.[1][2]

The disclosure, made in a regulatory filing, comes a day after rival Exxon Mobil issued a similar update showing the Iran war's dual impact on the world's largest oil producers: surging prices that pad upstream profits, offset by physical disruptions to output across the Persian Gulf.[3][4]

items.title: IUCN lists emperor penguins as endangered over sea ice loss

featured_image.name: Accidental discovery reveals new climate threat to emperor penguins

items.description: The International Union for Conservation of Nature has officially listed emperor penguins as endangered on its Red List of Threatened Species, elevating the iconic Antarctic birds from their previous classification of "near threatened" in a move driven by climate-fueled sea ice loss. The update, announced Thursday, marks one of the most dramatic reclassifications for a polar species in recent years.[1][2]

items.title: New model suggests dark matter has two particle states

featured_image.name: Fermilab scientists to look for dark matter using quantum ...

items.description: A team of physicists has put forward a new framework suggesting dark matter may consist of two distinct particle states rather than one, offering a potential explanation for why gamma-ray signals observed at the center of the Milky Way have not appeared in smaller nearby galaxies. The paper, titled "dSph-obic dark matter," was published on Wednesday in the Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics by Asher Berlin, Joshua Foster, Dan Hooper, and Gordan Krnjaic, all affiliated with the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory.[1][2]

items.title: Goldman Sachs cuts gas forecast after ceasefire but warns risks remain

featured_image.name: Natural gas, LNG prices soar on Middle East supply fears - CNBC

items.description: Goldman Sachs has warned that global natural gas markets face a prolonged supply shock stemming from Iranian attacks on Qatar's liquefied natural gas infrastructure, even as a fragile two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran offers temporary relief. The bank said in an April 2 research note that European gas prices could surge to 75–100 euros per megawatt-hour — roughly double recent levels — if disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz persist beyond April.[1]

items.title: Dow surges over 1,300 points after U.S.-Iran ceasefire

featured_image.name: Stock market news for April 8, 2026 - CNBC

items.description: U.S. stocks surged on Wednesday in their best session in a year after the United States and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire, raising hopes that a crippling oil shortage could begin to ease. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 1,325 points, or 2.85%, while the S&P 500 climbed 2.5% and the Nasdaq Composite rose as much as 3.5%. It was the Dow's largest single-day gain since April 2025, when markets rallied after a tariff pause.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump threatens to resume strikes if Iran breaks ceasefire

featured_image.name: President Trump’s ceasefire with Iran draws praise from world leaders

items.description:
President Donald Trump late on Wednesday warned that all American military forces deployed near Iran will remain in position and threatened to resume hostilities unless Tehran fully complies with the terms of a fragile ceasefire agreement reached just a day earlier.

"All US ships, aircraft and military personnel — with additional ammunition, weaponry and anything else that is appropriate and necessary for the lethal prosecution and destruction of an already substantially degraded enemy, will remain in place in and around Iran until such time as the REAL AGREEMENT reached is fully complied with," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform shortly before midnight Eastern time.[1]

He added: "If for any reason it is not, which is highly unlikely, then the 'shooting starts' bigger and better, and stronger than anyone has ever seen before".[1]

items.title: Artemis II crew races toward Friday splashdown after moon flyby

featured_image.name: Artemis II Launches Manned Test Flight Around The Moon

items.description: Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen is making history as the first non-American to travel beyond low Earth orbit, riding aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft on the Artemis II mission as the crew speeds back toward Earth after a flyby of the Moon. The 10-day mission, which launched on April 1 from Kennedy Space Center in Florida, marks the first crewed lunar voyage since Apollo 17 in 1972.[1][2]
